{{Short description|Theorem in Mathematics}}'''Halanay inequality''' is a [[Comparison theorem#Differential equations|comparison theorem]] for [[Delay differential equation|differential equations with delay]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Halanay |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YThILEV5ZPIC |title=Differential Equations: Stability, Oscillations, Time Lags |date=1966 |publisher=Academic Press |isbn=978-0-08-095529-2 |pages=378 |language=en}}</ref> This inequality and its generalizations have been applied to analyze the [[Stability theory|stability]] of delayed differential equations, and in particular, the stability of industrial processes with dead-time<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bresch-Pietri |first1=D. |last2=Chauvin |first2=J. |last3=Petit |first3=N. |date=2012 |title=Invoking Halanay inequality to conclude on closed-loop stability of a process with input-varying delay1 |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S1474667015347340 |journal=IFAC Proceedings Volumes |language=en |volume=45 |issue=14 |pages=266–271 |doi=10.3182/20120622-3-US-4021.00011|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and delayed neural networks.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Chen |first=Tianping |date=2001 |title=Global exponential stability of delayed Hopfield neural networks |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0893608001000594 |journal=Neural Networks |language=en |volume=14 |issue=8 |pages=977–980 |doi=10.1016/S0893-6080(01)00059-4|pmid=11681757 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Li |first1=Hongfei |last2=Li |first2=Chuandong |last3=Zhang |first3=Wei |last4=Xu |first4=Jing |date=2018 |title=Global Dissipativity of Inertial Neural Networks with Proportional Delay via New Generalized Halanay Inequalities |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s11063-018-9788-6 |journal=Neural Processing Letters |language=en |volume=48 |issue=3 |pages=1543–1561 |doi=10.1007/s11063-018-9788-6 |s2cid=34828185 |issn=1370-4621|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Statement ==

Let <math>t_{0}</math> be a real number and <math>\tau</math> be a non-negative number. If <math>v: [t_{0}-\tau, \infty) \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{+}</math> satisfies 
<math display="block">\frac{d}{dt} v(t) \leq-\alpha v(t)+\beta\left[\sup _{s \in[t-\tau, t]} v(s)\right],  t \geq t_{0} </math>
where <math>\alpha</math> and <math>\beta</math> are constants with <math>\alpha>\beta>0</math>, then 
<math display="block">v(t) \leq k e^{-\eta\left(t-t_{0}\right)}, t \geq t_{0}</math>
where <math>k>0</math> and <math>\eta>0</math>.
